newsitem.title: USA: MCI Q2 net hurt by slower LD revs growth.
newsitem.headline: MCI Q2 net hurt by slower LD revs growth.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp reported second quarter earnings slightly below the same quarter of last year, as the company saw slower revenue growth in long-distance and delays in entering local markets.

MCI reported second quarter net income of $280 million, or $0.40 per share, down from the year ago quarter's $300 million, or $0.43 per share, but in line with the company's expectations as pre-announced on July 10.
The second quarter consensus forecast among Wall Street analysts was $0.40 per share, according to First Call.
Second quarter revenues grew to $4.8 billion, up six percent over last year's second quarter.

Revenue in MCI's long distance business reached $4.4 billion, an increase of $195 million over second quarter 1996 results and in line with the company's previous guidance that long distance revenues would see four to five percent growth.

Revenue from ventures and developing markets like systems integration, wireless and local services grew about 29 percent to $613 million. Investments in new ventures and markets diluted second quarter earnings by $0.16 per share, it said.

From a small base, MCI's local revenue rose to $80 million, up 82 percent from second quarter 1996, but were slowed by ongoing regulatory hurdles the company has complained it faces in entering U.S. local phone markets.

"MCI is the best positioned long distance company to gain local market share, but policy makers must first enforce compliance with the Telecommunications Act of 1996," said Timothy Price, MCI president and chief operating officer.
Long distance traffic for the second quarter was up 5.5 percent year-over-year.
MCI's Business Markets unit again posted double digit revenue growth, despite a continued de-emphasis on the carrier channel.

Sales of networkMCI One, a business service that integrates long distance, wireless, Internet and local services into one customer service and billing system continued to drive growth, the company said.
More than two-thirds of MCI's business revenue comes from customers using four or more services and customer churn is at an all-time low, it said.

In the mass market segment, the company's flagship consumer service, MCI One, grew 50 percent in the last three months reaching the 3 million customer milestone. MCI said 85 percent of new MCI One sales came from non-MCI customers.
Regional long-distance calls, known in industry jargon as intraLATA, grew 30 percent in terms of minutes year-over-year.

On July 10, MCI said the anti-competitive practices of the local phone companies and the lack of compliance and enforcement of the Telecommunications Act of 1996 would result in local market losses twice what was originally planned and hurt its core business.
Second quarter revenue for MCI's ventures and developing markets segment increased 29 percent, to $613 million, from $477 million last year, and 6 percent sequentially.

MCI's Information Technology business, which primarily consists of MCI Systemhouse, the company's global systems integration unit, reported revenue of $444 million, a gain of 34 percent over last year's second quarter.

Second quarter wireless revenue was $83 million, up from $75 million in the first quarter. In the cellular market, MCI offered services in 47 U.S. markets and had nearly 434,000 customers, up 11 percent over second quarter last year.
